checks.q: Which statement best applies the lesson “Why attackers attack”?
checks.correct: Money, information theft, curiosity/fun, and hacktivism
distractors: Only hardware failure and weather
Faster software and lower costs
Backups, patching, and encryption
checks.teach: The same phishing technique could support different motives. A criminal may want money, while a state-sponsored group may want confidential research.
checks.answer: Money, information theft, curiosity/fun, and hacktivism

checks.q: Which statement best applies the lesson “Stuxnet as a defense lesson”?
checks.correct: It linked a computer compromise to manipulated physical equipment
distractors: It was only a website advertisement
It proved isolated systems need no host defenses
It was a password manager for industrial users
checks.teach: Stuxnet spread broadly but activated its damaging behavior only when it found the intended Siemens industrial setup. That distinction separates spreading from the final objective.
checks.answer: It linked a computer compromise to manipulated physical equipment

checks.q: Which statement best applies the lesson “Virtual machines and safe labs”?
checks.correct: Run isolated guest systems and restore earlier snapshots
distractors: Convert every attack into harmless text
Guarantee malware can never leave a guest
Replace the need for backups on production systems
checks.teach: A snapshot records a VM state before a lab. After analyzing a sample in an authorized lab, the student can revert instead of rebuilding everything.
checks.answer: Run isolated guest systems and restore earlier snapshots

checks.q: Which statement best applies the lesson “Defense as a process”?
checks.correct: Use several coordinated safeguards to prevent, detect, investigate, and recover
distractors: Purchase one security product and stop monitoring
Focus only on attacks that already succeeded
Remove all users from every computer
checks.teach: A firewall may block an unwanted connection, but a defender still needs host safeguards, logs, user education, and a response plan.
checks.answer: Use several coordinated safeguards to prevent, detect, investigate, and recover

checks.q: Which statement best applies the lesson “Defense in depth and risk”?
checks.correct: One missed attack can still meet another independent safeguard
distractors: Every safeguard detects exactly the same event
Multiple safeguards eliminate all residual risk
Security budgets do not affect architecture
checks.teach: If a malicious attachment reaches a laptop, limited privileges and application controls may still stop it after an email filter missed it.
checks.answer: One missed attack can still meet another independent safeguard

checks.q: Which statement best applies the lesson “Choke points and visibility”?
checks.correct: They create inspectable paths and useful views of network activity
distractors: They encrypt every stored file automatically
They remove the need for internal monitoring
They make every system use one password
checks.teach: Monitoring only the internet edge may miss traffic between two compromised internal computers. Internal sensors add another view.
checks.answer: They create inspectable paths and useful views of network activity

checks.q: Which statement best applies the lesson “Availability, scalability, and security”?
checks.correct: Security must work together with availability, growth, management, and cost
distractors: Security is the only design quality that matters
Availability means every user gets administrator rights
Scalability means removing traffic inspection
checks.teach: A security appliance that cannot handle peak traffic may become a bottleneck and reduce availability even when its filtering works.
checks.answer: Security must work together with availability, growth, management, and cost

checks.q: Which statement best applies the lesson “Firewalls and router ACLs”?
checks.correct: They enforce traffic rules at network boundaries
distractors: They guarantee that allowed applications contain no malware
They replace authentication inside every application
They store a complete copy of every packet forever
checks.teach: A rule may allow HTTPS from the internet to one public web server while blocking direct access to an internal database.
checks.answer: They enforce traffic rules at network boundaries

checks.q: Which statement best applies the lesson “IDS versus IPS”?
checks.correct: An IDS alerts; an IPS can also block traffic
distractors: An IDS encrypts while an IPS performs backups
An IDS runs only on laptops and an IPS only in clouds
An IDS allows all traffic and never records events
checks.teach: An IDS reports a suspicious exploit attempt for an analyst. An inline IPS can drop that traffic before it reaches the target.
checks.answer: An IDS alerts; an IPS can also block traffic

checks.q: Which statement best applies the lesson “Proxy servers”?
checks.correct: It evaluates and mediates user web requests
distractors: It assigns every computer a permanent MAC address
It proves every unblocked website is safe forever
It replaces disk encryption
checks.teach: When a user requests a known malware domain, the proxy can return a block page instead of retrieving the site.
checks.answer: It evaluates and mediates user web requests

checks.q: Which statement best applies the lesson “Host protection and application allowlisting”?
checks.correct: They use different evidence and policies to protect the endpoint
distractors: All three are names for the same firewall rule
All three only inspect traffic at the internet router
All three guarantee no false positives
checks.teach: A new unapproved executable may have no antivirus signature. Allowlisting can still prevent it from launching because it is absent from the approved list.
checks.answer: They use different evidence and policies to protect the endpoint

checks.q: Which statement best applies the lesson “Full packet capture versus flow data”?
checks.correct: Flow summarizes connections; packet capture can preserve packet-level detail
distractors: Flow contains every file while capture contains only IP addresses
Packet capture cannot support investigations
Flow automatically blocks every listed connection
checks.teach: Flow may show a laptop contacted a server for ten minutes. Packet capture may show the protocol details and unencrypted content exchanged during that connection.
checks.answer: Flow summarizes connections; packet capture can preserve packet-level detail

checks.q: Which statement best applies the lesson “DDoS, SYN floods, and Slowloris”?
checks.correct: They consume limited network or server capacity needed by real users
distractors: They secretly change database queries without affecting availability
They only work after a user reveals a password
They encrypt backups for confidentiality
checks.teach: A SYN flood sends many connection starts without completing the handshake. Slowloris sends enough partial data to keep sessions waiting.
checks.answer: They consume limited network or server capacity needed by real users

checks.q: Which statement best applies the lesson “SQL injection”?
checks.correct: The application mixes untrusted input into a database command
distractors: The database has too many encrypted backups
A router uses a long ACL
A user opens two browser tabs
checks.teach: A login value should become a data parameter. Concatenating it into a SQL command may let crafted text change the command’s meaning.
checks.answer: The application mixes untrusted input into a database command

checks.q: Which statement best applies the lesson “Cross-site scripting”?
checks.correct: A trusted page causes a browser to execute attacker-controlled script
distractors: A router runs out of cable ports
A disk uses full encryption
A DNS server assigns a local address
checks.teach: A comment field stores attacker-controlled script. When another user views the comment, the browser may run it as part of the site.
checks.answer: A trusted page causes a browser to execute attacker-controlled script

checks.q: Which statement best applies the lesson “Website defacement”?
checks.correct: An attacker changes site content without authorization
distractors: A user changes browser zoom
A server compresses an image
A company publishes an approved redesign
checks.teach: An attacker gains access to a content-management account and replaces the homepage. The visual change is the symptom; the account compromise is the access path.
checks.answer: An attacker changes site content without authorization

checks.q: Which statement best applies the lesson “Advance-fee and 419 scams”?
checks.correct: It promises a benefit and then requests money or sensitive information
distractors: It patches a workstation automatically
It blocks a website category at a proxy
It encrypts a legitimate bank transfer
checks.teach: A false lottery notice asks for contact information first, then later demands a processing payment. The staged requests lower suspicion.
checks.answer: It promises a benefit and then requests money or sensitive information

checks.q: Which statement best applies the lesson “Attack, vulnerability, and defense”?
checks.correct: The weakness determines which safeguard can interrupt the attack path
distractors: Every attack uses the same software weakness
A visible symptom always reveals the root cause
Defenses only matter after data is stolen
checks.teach: SQL injection is an attack technique. Unsafe query construction is the vulnerability. Parameterized queries address that weakness.
checks.answer: The weakness determines which safeguard can interrupt the attack path

checks.q: Which statement best applies the lesson “Phishing, smishing, and vishing”?
checks.correct: It uses deception to make a person take an unsafe action
distractors: It passively records every packet on a switch
It automatically patches a browser
It verifies a digital signature
checks.teach: A message impersonates payroll and links to a false login page. The attacker wants the victim to supply credentials.
checks.answer: It uses deception to make a person take an unsafe action

checks.q: Which statement best applies the lesson “Spear phishing”?
checks.correct: It is tailored to a specific person or small group
distractors: It can only be delivered by postal mail
It never includes a link or attachment
It is an untargeted message sent identically to everyone
checks.teach: A forged message to one finance employee refers to a real executive and current vendor. The specificity makes the request more believable.
checks.answer: It is tailored to a specific person or small group

checks.q: Which statement best applies the lesson “Email headers and investigation”?
checks.correct: The technical path and authentication evidence associated with delivery
distractors: The sender’s intent with absolute certainty
Every file the sender has ever opened
The recipient’s operating-system password
checks.teach: A display name says “Payroll,” while authentication results and the sending domain point elsewhere. That mismatch supports further investigation.
checks.answer: The technical path and authentication evidence associated with delivery

checks.q: Which statement best applies the lesson “Responding safely to suspicious messages”?
checks.correct: Use a trusted channel obtained independently of the message
distractors: Reply and ask whether the sender is malicious
Open the link if the logo looks correct
Disable antivirus before opening the attachment
checks.teach: A banking message says an account is locked. Open the bank’s known app instead of using the message link.
checks.answer: Use a trusted channel obtained independently of the message

checks.q: Which statement best applies the lesson “Fake antivirus and scareware”?
checks.correct: It invents or exaggerates danger to trigger installation or payment
distractors: It quietly improves disk performance for free
It is an operating-system patch from every vendor
It verifies that a website certificate is valid
checks.teach: A browser pop-up announces hundreds of infections and demands immediate payment. A webpage cannot be trusted simply because it resembles a system scanner.
checks.answer: It invents or exaggerates danger to trigger installation or payment

checks.q: Which statement best applies the lesson “Fake disk tools”?
checks.correct: It uses false system errors to sell or install an unsafe product
distractors: It reorganizes approved files under administrator supervision
It creates a verified offline backup
It checks a signed operating-system update
checks.teach: The program reports critical disk errors immediately after a user visits a suspicious site, even though it never performed a trustworthy scan.
checks.answer: It uses false system errors to sell or install an unsafe product

checks.q: Which statement best applies the lesson “User awareness and reconnaissance”?
checks.correct: Each can catch suspicious activity the other misses
distractors: Training makes mail filters unnecessary
A mail filter can determine every human intention
Reconnaissance only examines physical buildings
checks.teach: A filter allows a new sender. An employee notices the unusual payment request and calls the known manager instead of acting.
checks.answer: Each can catch suspicious activity the other misses

checks.q: Which statement best applies the lesson “Operating-system hardening”?
checks.correct: Reducing unnecessary exposure and strengthening required functions
distractors: Adding every optional service for future use
Giving all users administrator access
Disabling updates so settings never change
checks.teach: A workstation does not need a remote service, so an administrator disables it and closes the related listening port.
checks.answer: Reducing unnecessary exposure and strengthening required functions

checks.q: Which statement best applies the lesson “Patching safely”?
checks.correct: Testing can reveal compatibility or operational problems before production rollout
distractors: Testing proves attackers cannot use any future vulnerability
A tested patch never needs verification after installation
Testing replaces the need to obtain the patch from a trusted source
checks.teach: A security patch works on a test workstation but breaks a required legacy application. Testing reveals the compatibility problem before every employee is affected.
checks.answer: Testing can reveal compatibility or operational problems before production rollout

checks.q: Which statement best applies the lesson “Least privilege and reverse shells”?
checks.correct: Malicious code initially receives fewer powerful permissions
distractors: The account cannot connect to any network
The user automatically becomes an administrator during attacks
Every reverse shell uses an inbound blocked port only
checks.teach: A user can edit documents but cannot install a system driver. Malware launched by that user encounters the same permission boundary unless it exploits another weakness.
checks.answer: Malicious code initially receives fewer powerful permissions

checks.q: Which statement best applies the lesson “Services, updates, and host firewalls”?
checks.correct: They remove unused entry points and restrict access to required ones
distractors: They make passwords and account controls unnecessary
They guarantee every allowed service is free of bugs
They turn a workstation into a network router
checks.teach: A database server should not expose a file-sharing service nobody uses. Disable it rather than relying only on a perimeter firewall.
checks.answer: They remove unused entry points and restrict access to required ones

checks.q: Which statement best applies the lesson “Antivirus versus host IPS”?
checks.correct: They inspect different host evidence and can detect different suspicious behavior
distractors: They physically disconnect every infected cable
They replace all operating-system permissions
They only protect public websites
checks.teach: A host IPS rule alerts when an unusual program creates a file in a protected system folder. Antivirus may separately identify the file’s known malicious signature.
checks.answer: They inspect different host evidence and can detect different suspicious behavior

checks.q: Which statement best applies the lesson “Browser controls, hardening guides, and NAC”?
checks.correct: Use tested baselines and posture checks to keep devices within policy
distractors: Apply hundreds of settings at once without testing
Let users disable every safeguard permanently
Use NAC only to increase monitor brightness
checks.teach: A laptop missing required patches connects to the network. NAC places it in a restricted remediation area until it meets policy.
checks.answer: Use tested baselines and posture checks to keep devices within policy

checks.q: Which statement best applies the lesson “Website safety changes over time”?
checks.correct: Website content and third-party resources can change after an earlier scan
distractors: A domain name changes every second by definition
HTTPS guarantees all page content is harmless
A clean result deletes all future vulnerabilities
checks.teach: A news site is safe in the morning, then an attacker changes one included script in the afternoon. Yesterday’s scan cannot evaluate the new content.
checks.answer: Website content and third-party resources can change after an earlier scan

checks.q: Which statement best applies the lesson “Manual source review”?
checks.correct: Page code, embedded resources, redirects, and suspicious behavior
distractors: Only the color and font of the homepage
Only whether the domain uses HTTPS
The visitor’s private password database
checks.teach: A hidden iframe loads a newly registered external domain and starts a download. Those combined facts justify deeper isolated analysis.
checks.answer: Page code, embedded resources, redirects, and suspicious behavior

checks.q: Which statement best applies the lesson “Automated website analysis”?
checks.correct: They provide fast evidence but can miss new or conditional behavior
distractors: They guarantee a site stays safe forever
They make isolation unnecessary for suspicious content
They can determine a human attacker’s identity from the page color
checks.teach: Two scanners report no known malware, but the site only delivers harmful code to one browser version. The scan reduces uncertainty without eliminating it.
checks.answer: They provide fast evidence but can miss new or conditional behavior

checks.q: Which statement best applies the lesson “Isolated dynamic testing”?
checks.correct: It contains the experiment and lets the analyst observe system changes
distractors: It guarantees legal authorization for any website
It makes malware unable to contact any network automatically
It proves a clean host needs no backup
checks.teach: The analyst opens a suspect page in a disposable guest, records its outbound connections, and reverts to the clean snapshot after collecting evidence.
checks.answer: It contains the experiment and lets the analyst observe system changes

checks.q: Which statement best applies the lesson “Safe investigation decisions”?
checks.correct: Define the question and use the least risky authorized method
distractors: Open it on a production administrator workstation
Forward it to coworkers to compare results
Enter a real password to see whether login works
checks.teach: A user reports a suspicious link. The analyst checks the message and approved intelligence sources before deciding whether a controlled visit adds value.
checks.answer: Define the question and use the least risky authorized method

checks.q: Which statement best applies the lesson “Encryption vocabulary”?
checks.correct: A cipher and key transform plaintext into ciphertext
distractors: A hash key converts ciphertext directly into a password
Plaintext is already unreadable encrypted output
Decryption permanently destroys all original data
checks.teach: A file begins as readable plaintext. Encryption transforms it into ciphertext. An authorized recipient uses the required key to decrypt it.
checks.answer: A cipher and key transform plaintext into ciphertext

checks.q: Which statement best applies the lesson “What cryptography can protect”?
checks.correct: Confidentiality, integrity, authentication, and related assurances
distractors: Unlimited availability with no redundancy
Physical cooling for every server
Automatic deletion of every backup
checks.teach: Encryption protects a stored file’s confidentiality. A verified digital signature can support integrity, sender authentication, and non-repudiation.
checks.answer: Confidentiality, integrity, authentication, and related assurances

checks.q: Which statement best applies the lesson “Hashing and collisions”?
checks.correct: It creates a fixed-length digest used to compare data
distractors: It creates ciphertext that every user can decrypt without a key
It guarantees two inputs can never share a digest
It compresses a file and stores every original byte
checks.teach: A vendor publishes a trusted file hash. After download, you compute the file’s hash and compare it with the trusted value to detect alteration.
checks.answer: It creates a fixed-length digest used to compare data

checks.q: Which statement best applies the lesson “Stream and block ciphers”?
checks.correct: A stream cipher handles a stream in small units; a block cipher handles fixed-size blocks
distractors: A stream cipher hashes while a block cipher stores plaintext
A block cipher never uses a key
A stream cipher can only protect images
checks.teach: A block cipher may need a defined mode to protect a message longer than one block. Reusing a nonce in a mode that requires uniqueness can break security.
checks.answer: A stream cipher handles a stream in small units; a block cipher handles fixed-size blocks

checks.q: Which statement best applies the lesson “Symmetric encryption”?
checks.correct: The authorized parties use the same shared secret key
distractors: Everyone encrypts with a public key and only a private key decrypts
No key is required after installation
The digest is reversed to recover plaintext
checks.teach: A disk-encryption system uses a symmetric data-encryption key because large files must be processed efficiently.
checks.answer: The authorized parties use the same shared secret key

checks.q: Which statement best applies the lesson “Asymmetric encryption and signatures”?
checks.correct: The private key signs and the corresponding public key verifies
distractors: The public key must stay secret while the private key is posted
Both keys are identical copies
A signature automatically encrypts every signed message
checks.teach: A software vendor signs an update with its private key. A device uses the vendor’s trusted public key to verify the signature before installation.
checks.answer: The private key signs and the corresponding public key verifies

checks.q: Which statement best applies the lesson “Cryptographic attacks and downgrade risk”?
checks.correct: It forces communication to use an older weaker security option
distractors: It adds a longer key to every connection
It restores a VM snapshot
It finds a website through DNS
checks.teach: A client and server both support a modern protocol, but an attacker interferes so they negotiate an obsolete version with known weaknesses.
checks.answer: It forces communication to use an older weaker security option

checks.q: Which statement best applies the lesson “Software and hardware encryption”?
checks.correct: At file, disk, device, database, and communication layers
distractors: Only inside public web pages
Only after data has been deleted
Only on computers without operating systems
checks.teach: Full-disk encryption protects a stolen powered-off laptop, but an already unlocked laptop may expose files to the signed-in user or running malware.
checks.answer: At file, disk, device, database, and communication layers

checks.q: Which statement best applies the lesson “Blocks, hash pointers, and Merkle trees”?
checks.correct: Each block references prior data with hashes and summarizes transactions with a Merkle root
distractors: Every block stores only an unencrypted password
One central spreadsheet decides all peer actions
A hash pointer hides every transaction from all participants
checks.teach: To prove a transaction belongs to a block, a node can provide the transaction and a path of neighboring hashes leading to the recorded Merkle root.
checks.answer: Each block references prior data with hashes and summarizes transactions with a Merkle root

checks.q: Which statement best applies the lesson “Consensus, mining, forks, and P2P”?
checks.correct: It gives nodes rules for selecting a shared accepted history
distractors: It makes every transaction legal automatically
It prevents all software changes
It stores every private key in one central node
checks.teach: Two miners publish blocks at similar times. Nodes follow the protocol’s chain-selection rule until one history gains the required preference.
checks.answer: It gives nodes rules for selecting a shared accepted history

checks.q: Which statement best applies the lesson “Packets, TCP, and IP”?
checks.correct: IP routes packets; TCP provides reliable ordered transport
distractors: TCP assigns website names while IP encrypts disks
IP guarantees application authentication
TCP stores every packet permanently
checks.teach: A browser sends data through TCP. IP routers forward the resulting packets. The receiver’s TCP reorders data and detects missing portions for retransmission.
checks.answer: IP routes packets; TCP provides reliable ordered transport

checks.q: Which statement best applies the lesson “Spoofing, scanning, and Wireshark”?
checks.correct: Protocol fields and timing for traffic visible at the capture point
distractors: Every event on networks the interface cannot observe
The real human identity behind every IP address
Plaintext from every encrypted session without keys
checks.teach: Repeated SYN packets to many ports may indicate scanning. The pattern supports an interpretation when combined with context and logs.
checks.answer: Protocol fields and timing for traffic visible at the capture point

checks.q: Which statement best applies the lesson “TCP/IP protocols and security”?
checks.correct: Protocols define how services communicate and what protections they provide
distractors: Every application protocol automatically encrypts data
Protocols only affect physical cables
One port number proves the user’s identity
checks.teach: FTP can transfer files but sends sensitive information without encryption in its basic form. A secure alternative changes the protection of the connection.
checks.answer: Protocols define how services communicate and what protections they provide

checks.q: Which statement best applies the lesson “SNMP and ICMP”?
checks.correct: SNMP reads management data; ICMP supports reachability and network diagnostics
distractors: SNMP transfers email while ICMP encrypts disks
ICMP manages device configuration databases
They are two names for HTTPS
checks.teach: A monitoring system uses SNMP to read interface counters and CPU use, while ping checks whether the device responds and how long replies take.
checks.answer: SNMP reads management data; ICMP supports reachability and network diagnostics

checks.q: Which statement best applies the lesson “DNS and DNSSEC”?
checks.correct: It helps resolvers detect forged or altered DNS answers
distractors: It hides every DNS query from the network
It scans the destination for malware
It assigns administrator rights to domain owners
checks.teach: An attacker supplies a false address for a bank name. A validating resolver rejects the answer when its signature chain does not verify.
checks.answer: It helps resolvers detect forged or altered DNS answers

checks.q: Which statement best applies the lesson “FTP, FTPS, and secure file transfer”?
checks.correct: Basic FTP transmits credentials and content without encryption
distractors: FTP automatically signs every transferred file
FTP uses full-disk encryption for the server
FTP prevents all man-in-the-middle attacks
checks.teach: A user sends a password over basic FTP on an untrusted network. Someone capturing the traffic may read it.
checks.answer: Basic FTP transmits credentials and content without encryption

checks.q: Which statement best applies the lesson “Secure email and application protocols”?
checks.correct: HTTPS for web, SSH for remote administration, and S/MIME for protected email content
distractors: FTP for password secrecy and HTTP for private web traffic
ICMP for email encryption and DNS for disk encryption
SNMPv1 for private file transfer
checks.teach: An administrator uses SSH instead of Telnet so credentials and commands are not sent as readable plaintext.
checks.answer: HTTPS for web, SSH for remote administration, and S/MIME for protected email content

checks.q: Which statement best applies the lesson “Placement of security devices”?
checks.correct: A control needs to sit on or observe the relevant traffic path
distractors: Every network location sees identical traffic
Placement only changes the color of a diagram
A sensor can reconstruct packets that never reached it
checks.teach: A sensor placed outside encryption termination sees encrypted bytes. A sensor after termination may inspect the application traffic, subject to privacy and access policy.
checks.answer: A control needs to sit on or observe the relevant traffic path

checks.q: Which statement best applies the lesson “Security logs and centralized analysis”?
checks.correct: They preserve event evidence that can be correlated into a timeline
distractors: They prevent every logged attack automatically
They prove a failed login caused data theft
They replace the need to synchronize clocks
checks.teach: A firewall shows an inbound connection, an application log shows a failed login, and an audit log identifies the account action. Together they create a stronger timeline.
checks.answer: They preserve event evidence that can be correlated into a timeline

checks.q: Which statement best applies the lesson “Virtualization security”?
checks.correct: Virtualization improves isolation and recovery but concentrates new risks in hosts and hypervisors
distractors: Virtual machines require no patches
A Type 2 hypervisor has no host operating system
Snapshots guarantee off-site disaster recovery
checks.teach: Ten server VMs share one physical host. Efficient management improves, but a host failure or hypervisor compromise can affect several services.
checks.answer: Virtualization improves isolation and recovery but concentrates new risks in hosts and hypervisors

checks.q: Which statement best applies the lesson “Cloud models and shared security”?
checks.correct: Some infrastructure duties shift, while customer data, identity, and configuration duties remain
distractors: The provider becomes responsible for every customer password choice
Cloud data no longer resides on computers
Using SaaS removes the need for access reviews
checks.teach: With SaaS, the provider runs the application platform, while the customer decides which employees may access confidential records and how data is classified.
checks.answer: Some infrastructure duties shift, while customer data, identity, and configuration duties remain

sorts.q: Build the TCP three-way handshake order
sorts.teach: A client requests a connection with SYN, the server acknowledges and responds with SYN-ACK, and the client completes setup with ACK.

sorts.q: Order a safe response to an unexpected account warning
items: Stop before using the supplied link
Open the known app or trusted address
sorts.teach: Independent verification keeps the suspicious message from controlling both the warning and the verification path.
Testing and approval come before broad installation; verification checks that the patch and required work both function.

sorts.q: Order an investigation of a suspicious website
items: Define the question and confirm authorization
Prepare an isolated environment if needed
Revert or clean the environment and report findings
sorts.teach: Start with the least risky evidence. Active interaction belongs in an approved isolated environment with a defined purpose.

cloze.q: An ____ alerts on suspicious traffic; an ____ can also block it.
distractors: ACL; FTP
IPS; IDS
FTP; ACL
cloze.teach: Monitoring only the internet edge may miss traffic between two compromised internal computers. Internal sensors add another view.

cloze.q: ____ summarizes connections; ____ can preserve packet contents.
distractors: DNS; NAC
full packet capture; flow data
NAC; DNS
cloze.teach: A rule may allow HTTPS from the internet to one public web server while blocking direct access to an internal database.

cloze.q: Unsafe database command construction can enable ____; unsafe browser output can enable ____.
distractors: DDoS; FDE
XSS; SQL injection
FDE; DDoS
cloze.teach: When a user requests a known malware domain, the proxy can return a block page instead of retrieving the site.

cloze.q: Broad deceptive messages are ____; targeted deceptive messages are ____.
distractors: hardening; hashing
spear phishing; phishing
hashing; hardening
cloze.teach: A comment field stores attacker-controlled script. When another user views the comment, the browser may run it as part of the site.

cloze.q: Give only necessary permissions through ____; reduce exposed functions through system ____.
distractors: spoofing; mining
hardening; least privilege
mining; spoofing
cloze.teach: A banking message says an account is locked. Open the bank’s known app instead of using the message link.

cloze.q: Readable data are ____; encrypted output is ____.
distractors: digest; payload
ciphertext; plaintext
payload; digest
cloze.teach: A host IPS rule alerts when an unusual program creates a file in a protected system folder. Antivirus may separately identify the file’s known malicious signature.

cloze.q: A ____ is one-way comparison output; ____ is reversible with the appropriate key.
distractors: DNS; encoding
encryption; hash
encoding; DNS
cloze.teach: A news site is safe in the morning, then an attacker changes one included script in the afternoon. Yesterday’s scan cannot evaluate the new content.

cloze.q: A ____ key creates a digital signature; the matching ____ key verifies it.
distractors: shared; session
public; private
session; shared
cloze.teach: The analyst opens a suspect page in a disposable guest, records its outbound connections, and reverts to the clean snapshot after collecting evidence.

cloze.q: ____ provides IP routing; ____ provides reliable ordered transport.
distractors: DNS; FTP
TCP; IP
FTP; DNS
cloze.teach: A block cipher may need a defined mode to protect a message longer than one block. Reusing a nonce in a mode that requires uniqueness can break security.

cloze.q: ____ monitors device statistics; ____ commonly tests reachability and timing.
distractors: SFTP; HTTPS
ICMP; SNMP
HTTPS; SFTP
cloze.teach: A software vendor signs an update with its private key. A device uses the vendor’s trusted public key to verify the signature before installation.

cloze.q: ____ protects FTP with TLS; ____ transfers files through SSH.
distractors: FTP; SRTP
SFTP; FTPS
SRTP; FTP
cloze.teach: Full-disk encryption protects a stolen powered-off laptop, but an already unlocked laptop may expose files to the signed-in user or running malware.
